text:
maria: Quick thread — proposal for edge-level soft quotas that can borrow from a global low-priority pool when a tenant's per-route soft limit is hit. Goal: keep tail latencies good for short bursts without immediately hitting hard central quota.

jon: Can you sketch the interface boundaries? who owns what?

maria: Edge owns soft accounting and immediate decisions. Central quota service owns hard limits, long-term reconciliation, and the canonical ledger. Edge can request short-lived borrow tokens from central. If denied, edge falls back to configured degrade behavior.

kevin: Abuse concern: a noisy tenant could repeatedly borrow and game the pool. We need cooldowns and per-tenant borrow budgets. Also audit logging for every borrow request.

quota-bot: :warning: AUTOMATED: Borrow request rate spike detected for tenant t-123 (42 req/s) — blocking until manual triage if repeated.

kevin: ^^ ops alert is useful. We should also surface borrow_denied alerts to sig-ops and rate-security.

sophie: Proposal: borrow policy configurable per-tenant and per-route. Defaults: micro-borrow local-only up to 10 tokens, macro-borrow (>=10) requires central ack. Borrows have TTL and are reconciled asynchronously. Also enforce a borrow-cooldown (exponential backoff).

maria: Tradeoffs: calling central synchronously on every burst kills p99. So micro-borrows are fast-path local decisions (risk: temporary oversubscribe). Macro-borrows are slower but safer. We need strong telemetry to detect divergence.

jon: Sketch of borrow API (HTTP/JSON):
```
POST /quota/borrow
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "tokens": 100,
  "ttl_ms": 5000
}
```
Central returns { allowed: true/false, granted: <int>, expires_at: <ts> }

kevin: Nice. Add fields for reason codes so edges can classify denials (OVERALL_CAPACITY, TENANT_COOLDOWN, POLICY_VIOLATION). Also attach a signed nonce so edges can prove they got an ack during reconciliation.

sophie: Metrics to add: borrow_request_rate, borrow_granted, borrow_denied, micro_borrows_local, oversubscribe_reconciliations, borrow_age_ms histogram. Dashboards by tenant and route.

maria: Abuse mitigation ideas:
- per-tenant daily borrow budget that resets slowly (decay window)
- burst score that increases with borrow frequency, triggers stricter denials
- require stronger auth for tenants that frequently borrow

jon: For correctness, reconciliation must be tolerant: central will periodically pull edge usage deltas and mark disputes. If edges over-consumed, we can deduct from future capacity or bill. Need to define safe window where we trust edge local decisions (e.g., 1s for micro-borrows).

kevin: Ops: also add a cluster-wide emergency circuit that can preempt and reject all borrows when overall utilization > 90% to prevent cascading. That circuit should be able to be toggled by SRE with a single flag.

maria: Implementation plan:
1) RFC doc with explicit API and policy knobs (this week)
2) Prototype micro-borrow fast-path in edge proxy (jon, 1 sprint)
3) Central endpoints + reconciliation worker (jon + kevin, 2nd sprint)
4) Canary in us-west on low-risk tenants -> monitor borrow metrics -> iterate

jon: I can own the prototype and initial central endpoints. Will open a PR for the API shape by EOD.

kevin: I'll own abuse heuristics and dashboards. Will draft a checklist for required metrics and alerts.

sophie: I'll write the policy templates for tenant config + a playbook for borrow-denied incidents.

maria: Sounds good. Quick checklist for the RFC: API schema, micro vs macro thresholds, borrow TTLs, cooldown/backoff, reconciliation cadence, billing/penalty semantics, emergency circuit controls.

jon: Adding: include traffic replay harness so we can simulate borrow storms in staging.

maria: @quota-bot please post a reminder to review the RFC in #eng-platform in 3 days. :thumbsup:

quota-bot: Reminder scheduled: review "edge borrow pool RFC" in #eng-platform in 3 days.

sophie: Thanks everyone — we'll iterate in the RFC thread.

kevin: SGTM. If someone can drop the initial API proto into the repo I'll review the security and billing implications.

maria: I'll put the RFC in the docs repo and tag you all. End of thread.
